fields.h1: Build a Salon Client Survey That Ends in One Change
fields.hero_description: Get a salon client survey that asks about the color, the cut, and the booking, and emails the owner each low score.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds for Salon Feedback
fields.features_subheading: Describe your services and team in a prompt. Emergent builds the survey and its alert emails, plus a results dashboard by stylist.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the service

The first screen asks which service the client had. A color client then rates how well the shade matched the request, and a cut client rates the shape. Change any question by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Sent the evening after the visit

The app reads finished appointments from your booking software through its API and emails each client the link that evening. A client seen twice in a month gets one survey.
fields.feature_3:
Low scores reach someone who can call

Set the score that needs a call back, such as 2 or lower on the color match. The app emails that answer and its comment to the person you name, with the client's phone number.
fields.feature_4:
A weekly digest for each stylist

Ask who did the service, and every chart can split by stylist. Each stylist can get a Monday email with only their own clients' answers, which suits a building of renters.
fields.feature_5:
One tap per screen on a phone

Clients answer one question per screen with large buttons, at the front desk or on the ride home. Emergent puts no cap on responses, whether 30 clients answer in a month or 3,000.
fields.feature_6:
Client answers in a database you own

Every answer is a row in a database you own, tagged with the date, the service, and the stylist. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep building.

fields.usecase_heading: What Four Salons Changed After Asking
fields.tab_content_1:
Low color scores trace back to a first balayage

Hollyhock Color Studio emails 4 questions after every color appointment. A color-match score of 2 or lower emails owner Paz Arriaga the client's comment. In August, 9 of 164 color clients scored that low, and 6 of the 9 had come in for a first balayage. She now books a 15-minute consultation before every first balayage.
fields.tab_content_2:
No weekend openings kept 26 of 64 clients away

Ninebark Salon sends 3 questions to any client who has not booked in 12 weeks. The first asks what kept them from booking. Of the 64 who answered this spring, 26 picked no weekend openings, ahead of price at 17, moving away at 12, and other reasons at 9. The salon now opens on Sundays from 10 to 4.
fields.tab_content_3:
Regulars pick a scalp treatment as the next service

Gilded Fern Hair Lounge had room for one new service and asked 300 regulars which they would book in the next 3 months. Of the 182 who answered, 71 chose a scalp treatment, 48 an express blowout, 39 keratin smoothing, and 24 brow lamination. The menu now lists a 30-minute scalp treatment after any cut.
fields.tab_content_4:
Parking rated 1 or 2 by 48 of 140 suite clients

Seven stylists rent suites at Brickyard Salon Suites, and one survey goes to all their clients. Each Monday, a renter's email holds answers from their clients alone. Building owner Della Haskins reads the parking question. In October, 48 of 140 clients rated parking 1 or 2, and she leased 4 spaces in the lot next door.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Salon Client Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to run a salon client survey that asks about each service and gets every low score a call back from the right person.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the answers can change
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask about the visit, not the hair
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Let the service pick the questions
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Send it the evening of the visit
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the decisions client answers could move: opening hours, consultation length, which service to add next. Drop any question that cannot change one of them. Give Emergent that list in your prompt, and the first draft of the survey follows it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask what the client saw and felt: the consultation, whether the result matched the request, the wait at the desk, and the price. Leave scalp and skin conditions to the intake form a stylist reads before the service, not a survey the owner reads after it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Open with one question about which service the client had, and fit the rest to that answer. Ask nail clients whether the set lasted the week, and keep toner questions for color clients. Nobody who came in for a blowout should see either one.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Send the link the same evening, while the client still remembers the chair and the checkout. Cap it at one survey per client per month, so a regular who books a weekly blowout is not asked the same questions four times.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Pick who calls back on low scores
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick one person for each kind of low score: the owner for the color match, the front desk lead for booking trouble. Set the score that triggers their email, 2 or lower for example, and agree to call the client within 2 business days.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Answer it yourself on a phone
fields.howto_step_6_des: Have two stylists answer the survey on their own phones before any client sees it. Time it, send a test score of 1 to check that it reaches the right inbox, and rewrite any question either of them had to read twice.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Once a quarter, put one change the answers led to on a card at the front desk and in the next survey email. Name what clients asked for and when it starts, such as Sunday hours from next month or a longer first consultation.

faq_plan.q: What is a salon client survey?
faq_plan.a: A salon client survey is a short set of questions a salon sends clients about a visit, such as the consultation, the result, the wait, and the price. The owner reads the answers to decide what to change and which client to call back after a bad visit.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a salon client survey?
faq_plan.a: Write one prompt for Emergent's AI survey builder that names your services and the score that should reach the owner. Emergent builds the survey and the database it fills, and a follow-up prompt adds a question or a weekly email. Start on the free tier, which covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What questions should I ask in a salon client survey?
faq_plan.a: Ask about the parts of the visit the salon controls. Cover how easy booking was, whether the stylist asked what the client wanted before starting, whether the result matched that request, and whether the price matched the quote. Add one question on whether the client plans to book again, and close with an open question on what to fix first.

faq_plan.q: How soon after an appointment should a salon client survey go out?
faq_plan.a: Send it that evening, a few hours after the client leaves the chair. A color studio can add one question a week later about how the shade looks after a few washes. The timing works like a restaurant survey: ask soon after the visit, and send no more than one reminder.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a salon client survey have?
faq_plan.a: Keep the survey after a routine visit to 4 or 5 questions: the service, the result, the booking, a rebook question, and one open comment. Save longer surveys, such as a vote on new services, for a few times a year. Emergent builds it as one question per screen, and a client answers each with one tap on a phone.

faq_plan.q: Should a salon client survey ask for the client's name?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as an optional field. A name lets the owner call back a client who scored the color match low, while an anonymous comment cannot get a reply. With the field optional, clients who want a call leave their name, and the rest still answer without one.

faq_plan.q: Should a salon client survey ask whether clients would recommend the salon?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as one question near the end. The question behind every nps survey asks how likely the client is to recommend you to a friend or colleague, and the Net Promoter System scores it on a zero-to-ten scale. Ask it the same way every month so the scores compare, and keep the rebook question beside it.

faq_plan.q: Can a salon client survey find out why clients stopped booking?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if it goes to overdue clients and asks them directly in 3 questions or fewer. Set overdue from each client's habit: a client booked every 5 weeks is overdue at 8, and a twice-a-year color client is not. Offer fixed reasons plus an other box to keep answers countable. With the booking system connected by API, the app sends the survey the day a client goes overdue.

faq_plan.q: Can a salon client survey ask happy clients to leave an online review?
faq_plan.a: Not only the happy ones. Google's policy for Maps reviews names selectively soliciting positive reviews from customers among the things merchants may not do. Put the review link on the thank-you screen every client sees, whatever score they gave, and keep low scores going to the owner for a call back.

faq_plan.q: How can a salon client survey compare feedback for each stylist?
faq_plan.a: Make the first question ask which stylist did the service, and every result can split by stylist. Keep the same rating questions for every chair, as in any customer satisfaction survey, and wait for about 20 answers per stylist before reading much into a gap. On Emergent, those answers sit in a database the salon owns.

plan.angle: Salon client survey results are thin: generic question lists and template galleries that end at the questions. This page shows four salons using a client survey to change one thing each: a color studio that emails its owner every low color-match score, a salon asking lapsed regulars why they stopped booking, a hair lounge letting regulars vote on its next service, and a suite building where each renter stylist gets only their own clients' answers while the owner reads the parking scores. The FAQ covers which questions to ask, when to send, length, names versus anonymity, a recommend question, lapsed clients, online reviews and comparing stylists; the how-to covers deciding what the answers can change and who replies to each low score.
tab_stories: Hollyhock Color Studio emails 4 questions the evening after every color appointment, a color-match score of 2 or lower emails owner Paz Arriaga the client's comment, and in August 9 of 164 color clients scored that low, 6 of them at a first balayage, so she now books a 15-minute consultation before every first balayage.

Ninebark Salon sends 3 questions to any client who has not booked in 12 weeks, 64 answered in the spring, 26 of them picked no weekend openings as the reason over price, a move or something else, and the salon now opens on Sundays from 10 to 4.

Gilded Fern Hair Lounge asks 300 regulars which of 4 new services they would book in the next 3 months, 182 answer, 71 pick a scalp treatment, and the lounge adds a 30-minute scalp treatment that can follow any cut.

Brickyard Salon Suites runs one survey for the clients of its 7 renter stylists, each stylist gets a weekly email with only their own clients' answers, and building owner Della Haskins reads the parking question, which 48 of 140 October clients rated 1 or 2, so she leased 4 spaces in the lot next door.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Salon Client Survey That Ends in One Change'; hero 'Get a salon client survey that asks about the color, the cut, and the booking, and emails the owner each low score.' states the whole job; how-to description is one sentence on what the steps achieve.

intent.evidence: No eligible PAA (all 20 AlsoAsked rejected PA3/PA6); page delivers questions to ask (FAQ 3), timing, length, a 7-step how-to and four worked salon examples (color, lapsed, new service, suites).

specificity.evidence: Salon vocabulary throughout: 'first balayage', 'toner questions for color clients', 'a building of renters', 'weekly blowout'. Table cells from the library (see note on 'employee engagement').

openers.evidence: Feature bodies open on full sentences ('The first screen asks which service the client had.', 'Set the score that needs a call back'); tabs open on the business doing something ('Ninebark Salon sends 3 questions').

craft.evidence: One ', so' ending (howto_step_4) under the cap; no run-on lists; sentences carry one idea.

voice.evidence: Reads operator-written: 'Have two stylists answer the survey on their own phones before any client sees it... send a test score of 1'. Link-bridge sentences noted, not blocking.

truth.evidence: Google: 'names selectively soliciting positive reviews from customers among the things merchants may not do' matches source span under 'We do not allow merchants to' (scope kept: Maps reviews, merchants). NPS: 'how likely ... to recommend you to a friend or colleague ... zero-to-ten scale' matches netpromotersystem.com. Emergent sentences map to prompt-build, api-connect, alerts, conversational, no-caps, database-owned, code-export, free-start. Numbers add: 26+17+12+9=64, 71+48+39+24=182, 6+2+1=9, 48+37+55=140.

distinct.evidence: Own angle (one change per survey) and salon-only stories; FAQ 9 shares its idea with dental-patient-survey (note), not blocking: wording differs and QC D2 passed.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic written questions, each answered first ('Send it that evening', 'Yes, as an optional field', 'Not only the happy ones'); hub link in item 2; 3 sibling links; 2 moat lines (FAQ 5, FAQ 10).

images.evidence: Contact sheet: tab 1 '9 of 164 color clients, August' / '6 of 9 low scores'; tab 2 '26 of 64 wanted weekends' / 'Sundays, 10 to 4'; tab 3 'Picked by 71 of 182'; tab 4 '48 of 140 rated it 1 or 2' / '4 spaces leased next door'; all match tab copy, one hero each.

findings.issue: FAQ 9 follows dental-patient-survey's online-review FAQ beat for beat with nouns swapped (question shape 'Can a ... survey ask happy X ... online review', 'Not for Google reviews' / 'Not only the happy ones', policy line, 'whatever score they gave', low scores handled separately). Not a copy (QC D2 passed, wording differs, both true), but the hub now carries the same answer twice.
findings.fix: If this page is reworked for another reason, give FAQ 9 a salon-specific beat (e.g. where the review link sits after a color appointment, or a stylist asking at checkout) instead of the dental page's structure.

findings.quote: The timing works like a restaurant survey: ask soon after the visit, and send no more than one reminder.
findings.issue: Two sibling links ride on bridge sentences written to hold the anchor: FAQ 4 'The timing works like a restaurant survey' and FAQ 10 'Keep the same rating questions for every chair, as in any customer satisfaction survey'. They read as inserted for the link, not for the salon owner.
findings.fix: Anchor the links where the sibling genuinely helps (e.g. 'a customer satisfaction survey' as the broader version of this survey) or pick siblings that fit the sentence.

findings.issue: 'nps' in lowercase mid-sentence reads as a typo; the acronym is NPS everywhere else on the web, including the source.
findings.fix: Anchor text 'NPS survey' (case-insensitive exact match) if the link checker allows it.

findings.quote: Ninebark Salon sends 3 questions to any client who has not booked in 12 weeks.

findings.fix: Either let the tab mention a per-client cutoff, or soften FAQ 8 to offer a flat cutoff as the simple option.
